title: Phase-aware kernel weigher for mixed prefill/decode workloads
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Goal: Build a lightweight, phase-aware kernel weigher that picks the most appropriate compute kernel for each request based on (1) hardware profile, (2) sequence-length bucket, and (3) token-phase (prefill vs decode). The weigher should: combine a compact cost model (latency median + tail risk penalty + compute cost) with phase hysteresis to avoid thrashing during short bursts; support small online probes for exploration; integrate a safety fallback so we never violate SLOs during exploration; and emit the signals necessary for offline tuning and model-level rollout gating.

Context: Existing kernel-pickers bias heavily on average throughput or static architecture heuristics and often switch kernels too aggressively when token-phase transitions (prefill -> decode) or when seq-len estimates are noisy. This causes latency spikes, increased tail latency, and lost tail-SLOs for latency-sensitive customers. We need a pragmatic autotune component that is inexpensive to run on the critical path and yet provides measurable latency/ cost improvements for mixed workloads (chat + long-context batching).

Non-goals: Replacing the full bandit/autodidactic explorer used in long batch experiments; implementing heavy-weight per-model neural cost predictors at rollout time. We aim for a pragmatic hybrid: simple analytic cost + lightweight online probing + safe rollback policy.
acceptance_criteria:
- Phase-aware scoring function implemented and exposed via runtime tracing for each decision (score components: baseline latency, 95th-tail penalty, token-cost estimate).
- Default weights tuned on historical trace (two target architectures: A100-40GB and L40s) with clear config for per-tenant overrides.
- Small-probe mechanism: 1% of requests allowed to sample alternative kernel under controlled budget.
- Safety guard: if sampled alternative causes >10% increase in 99th-percentile latency for the sampling cohort vs baseline in a rolling 5-minute window, that kernel is automatically blacklisted for that cohort.
- End-to-end testbench shows >=5% median latency improvement or >=7% cost reduction on at least one representative mixed workload trace while no SLO regressions at 99th percentile.
- Instrumentation: metrics emitted for decisions (chosen_kernel, score_components, sampled_flag, blacklist_events) and a dashboard tile showing choice distribution by seq-len bucket and phase.
- Design doc and PR merged, and a canary rollout to 3% traffic completed with monitoring alerts and rollback playbook validated.
